KeyPassages: 2 Samuel 22:30; Isaiah 35:6; Song of Solomon 2:8; Zephaniah 1:9; Psalms 18:29
BiblicalUsage: To leap is the joy of the lame made whole and the strength of the warrior, and the word carries both. David leaps over a wall by his God, the lame man in the desert shall leap as a hart when the wilderness breaks out in streams, and the beloved comes leaping upon the mountains. The same word turns dark when men leap on the threshold to fill their masters' houses with violence.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the leap pictures what God does for the weak: He does not teach us to climb the wall, He carries us over it. That is the joy of salvation, and it makes the lame sing.
